title: Heroes & Myths in Entrepreneurship -- Guy Raz

reader_summary.headline: Hi, everyone, welcome to the A6 and Z podcast.
reader_summary.overview: Hi, everyone, welcome to the A6 and Z podcast. I'm Sonal, and today we have a unique episode. It's someone whose work and latest theme of his work that we of course relate to. And it's Guy Raz, the host, co-creator and editorial director of three NPR programs, including How I Built This.

key_points.text: Guy has a new book coming out this week by the same name, How I Built This.
key_points.evidence_quote: Guy has a new book coming out this week by the same name, How I Built This, The Unexpected Paths to Success from the world's most inspiring entrepreneurs.

key_points.text: It's based on his interviews with all kinds of entrepreneurs, big and small, of all kinds of backgrounds and all kinds of businesses.
key_points.evidence_quote: It's based on his interviews with all kinds of entrepreneurs, big and small, of all kinds of backgrounds and all kinds of businesses.

key_points.text: He let each of them tell their unique stories on his show, but pulls a lot of common threads into this book.
key_points.evidence_quote: He let each of them tell their unique stories on his show, but pulls a lot of common threads into this book.

key_points.text: So we touch on a few of these threads, and especially one of my favorite themes throughout, that of storytelling, including movements, buzz, community.
key_points.evidence_quote: So we touch on a few of these threads, and especially one of my favorite themes throughout, that of storytelling, including movements, buzz, community, and more.

thesis: The episode discusses the narrative arc of the hero's journey as a framework for understanding entrepreneurial stories, emphasizing that most entrepreneurs mitigate risk rather than acting as kamikaze risk takers. It argues against the fetishization of failure, noting that while failure builds resilience, it is not a badge of honor for those without a safety net, and distinguishes between the scariness of the unknown and the danger of regretting inaction.
